name: Communicating online
intro: How to adapt your English to purpose, receiver and situation in digital communication, how to write a good email, netiquette, and how online communication differs from face-to-face communication.
sammendrag:
## Communicating in a digital world

Much of our communication today happens online: in chats, emails, comments, video calls and games. To communicate well, you must adapt your language to the **purpose** (why you write), the **receiver** (who reads it) and the **situation** (where and when).

## Formal and informal language

- **Informal** language is used with friends and family: short sentences, **contractions** (I'm, don't), slang, emojis and abbreviations like LOL or BRB.
- **Formal** language is used with teachers, employers or people you don't know: full sentences, polite phrases, correct spelling and no slang.

Choosing the right **register** shows respect and helps the receiver understand you.

## Writing a good email

A formal email usually has

- a clear **subject line**
- a **greeting**: Dear Ms Smith, / Hello Mr Jones,
- a short **introduction** explaining why you are writing
- the **main message**, with one idea per paragraph
- a polite **closing**: Kind regards, / Best wishes, followed by your name

Avoid writing only in capital letters – it looks like SHOUTING.

## Netiquette

**Netiquette** (net + etiquette) means good manners online:

- Think before you post. Would you say it face to face?
- Be polite, even when you disagree.
- Don't share other people's pictures or personal information without permission.
- Remember that tone of voice and body language are missing online, so jokes and irony can easily be misunderstood.

## Online versus offline communication

Communication online differs from face-to-face communication:

- It can be **asynchronous** – people answer when it suits them, as in email – or **synchronous**, like a video call.
- There are fewer **non-verbal cues**, such as facial expressions and tone of voice.
- People may feel **anonymous** and act differently than they would in real life.
- Messages can be **saved, screenshotted and shared**, so they may last for a very long time.

## Different ways of thinking

People from different cultures communicate in different ways. Some are **direct** and say exactly what they mean, while others are more **indirect** and careful. In English, words like **please**, **thank you** and **sorry**, and phrases like **Could you …?** or **Would you mind …?**, are very important. Being aware of such differences helps you avoid misunderstandings when you talk to people around the world, for example in online games or international school projects.

flashcards.def: Why a text is written, for example to inform, ask or entertain.
The person or group who reads or listens to a message.
How formal or informal your language is.
Relaxed language used with friends: contractions, slang and emojis.
Polite, correct language used with teachers, employers and strangers.
A short form of two words, like don't (do not) or I'm (I am).
A short line that tells the receiver what an email is about.
How you start a letter or email, like “Dear Ms Smith,”.
How you end a formal email, like “Kind regards,” followed by your name.
Communication where people answer when it suits them, like email.
Communication in real time, like a video call or a live chat.
Facial expressions, tone of voice and body language.
Expressing yourself more carefully and politely, often with hints.

options: How polite your message sounds
How formal or informal your language is
How quickly you answer an online message
How clearly you explain the main idea
quiz.explain: You choose your register depending on who you are talking to.

quiz.text: Which greeting fits a formal email to a teacher?
options: Hey dude!
Yo!
Sup
Dear Ms Smith,
quiz.explain: Formal emails start with a polite greeting and the person's name.

options: Good manners online
A computer program
Online privacy settings
An email writing style

quiz.text: Which is an example of informal language?
options: I would appreciate a quick reply.
Please let me know your decision.
lol brb, gonna grab food
I look forward to your response.
quiz.explain: Abbreviations and slang are typical of informal chat.

quiz.text: Why can jokes easily be misunderstood online?
options: Because online messages are usually sent in another language
Because websites change jokes into formal language
Because tone of voice and body language are missing
Because jokes are usually shared through email
quiz.explain: Without non-verbal cues, irony can be taken seriously.

options: People reply at a time that works for them, like email
People talk at the same time during a live video call
People speak together during a face-to-face conversation
People answer at once during a phone conversation
quiz.explain: The other options happen in real time.

quiz.text: Why should you avoid writing only in capital letters?
options: People read it as a spelling mistake
People read it as an email address
People read it as a password
People read it as shouting
quiz.explain: Capital letters are read as a raised voice online.

quiz.text: Which phrase is a polite way to ask for something in English?
options: Send me the file right now.
Could you help me, please?
You need to help me today.
I expect you to reply soon.
quiz.explain: “Could you” and “please” make a request polite.

quiz.text: Why should you think before you post?
options: Because messages can be saved and shared and last a long time
Because every post is checked by teachers before it appears
Because deleting a post removes every saved copy
Because only friends can see what you post online
quiz.explain: Screenshots can spread even if you delete a post.

quiz.text: What is the difference between direct and indirect communication?
options: Direct communication uses spoken words; indirect communication uses written words
Direct communication is formal and polite; indirect communication is informal and casual
Direct communication is for close friends; indirect communication is for teachers
Direct means saying exactly what you mean; indirect means expressing yourself more carefully and politely
quiz.explain: Cultures often differ in how direct people are.

ekstra.text: It is fine to use slang in a job application email.
ekstra.explain: A job application should be written in formal language.

ekstra.text: Online, you have fewer non-verbal cues than face to face.
ekstra.explain: Facial expressions and tone of voice are often missing.

ekstra.text: A good email should have a clear subject line.
ekstra.explain: The subject line tells the receiver what the email is about.

ekstra.text: People always behave the same online as they do offline.
ekstra.explain: Feeling anonymous can make people act differently.

ekstra.text: Which closing fits a formal email?
options: See you,
Kind regards,
Talk soon,
Bye then,
ekstra.explain: “Kind regards” and “Best wishes” are polite closings.

ekstra.text: What is the purpose of a text?
options: The reason the text was written
The main idea in the text
The person who reads the text
The place where the text appears
ekstra.explain: Purpose, receiver and situation decide how you write.

ekstra.text: Which of these is a contraction?
options: doesnt
didnt
don't
wouldnt
ekstra.explain: A contraction combines two words with an apostrophe.

skriv.text: You need to tell your teacher that you will miss a lesson, and later tell a close friend the same news in a chat. Explain one way your language should differ in each message, and why.
skriv.fasit: I would use polite, formal language with my teacher because the receiver is a teacher. I could use more relaxed, informal language with my friend.
kriterier: Explains that the message to the teacher should be formal or polite and the message to the friend can be informal.
Connects the choice of language to who will receive the message.

skriv.text: Rewrite this as a polite, formal request to your teacher: “hey, can u send me the homework? thx”
skriv.fasit: Could you please send me the homework? Thank you.
kriterier: Uses polite wording to make the request.
Uses correct spelling and avoids slang or informal abbreviations.

skriv.text: Compare an email and a video call. Explain how the timing of replies differs in these two types of communication.
skriv.fasit: An email is asynchronous, so people can reply when it suits them. A video call is synchronous, so people communicate in real time.
kriterier: Explains that email replies do not have to happen straight away.
Explains that a video call happens in real time.

skriv.text: Explain what a contraction is and give one example.
skriv.fasit: A contraction is a shortened form of two words. For example, “I'm” is short for “I am.”
kriterier: Explains that a contraction is a short form made from two words.
Gives a correct example and its full form.

skriv.text: A friend sends you a photo of someone else and asks you to share it in a group chat. What should you do before sharing it, and why?
skriv.fasit: I should ask the person in the photo for permission first. Sharing someone’s picture without permission does not respect their privacy.
kriterier: Says to get permission from the person in the photo before sharing it.
Explains that this protects the person’s privacy or respects their choice.

skriv.text: In a text chat, you cannot see the other person’s face or hear their voice. Name two non-verbal cues that are missing and explain one thing this can make harder.
skriv.fasit: Facial expressions and tone of voice are missing. This can make it harder to understand how someone feels or what they mean.
kriterier: Names two relevant non-verbal cues, such as facial expressions, tone of voice or body language.
Explains that missing cues can make feelings or meaning harder to understand.

skriv.text: In an online school project, one student says exactly what they think, while another expresses ideas carefully and gives hints. Explain how recognising these different communication styles could help them work together.
skriv.fasit: One student is communicating directly, while the other is communicating indirectly. Recognising this can help them avoid misunderstandings and understand each other’s intentions.
kriterier: Identifies the first style as direct and the second as indirect, or explains the difference accurately.
Explains how noticing the different styles can help avoid misunderstandings or improve understanding.

skriv.text: You are writing a formal email about a missed assignment. Why should you put only one main idea in each paragraph of the main message?
skriv.fasit: Putting one main idea in each paragraph makes the email easier to follow. The receiver can understand the message more clearly.
kriterier: Explains that separate paragraphs organise the ideas.
Connects this organisation to making the email easier for the receiver to understand.
